finding.claim: HIGH: The unauthenticated POST /hooks/test route passes req.body.callback straight to axios.post. The attacker picks the full URL (scheme, host, port, path), and nothing validates it. axios follows redirects by default, so even an allowlist-less external target could bounce to internal addresses. The response status is returned to the caller, so the attacker can probe internal services, ports, and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254). The POST body is fixed to {ping:true}, so the attacker does not control the request body.
finding.source: req.body.callback (POST body field on the public router `pub`)

trace.note: `pub` router is defined with no auth middleware (requireAdmin is applied only to `admin` at line 12)
req.body.callback is used unmodified as the URL for axios.post
r.status is returned in the JSON response, which makes this a non-blind SSRF oracle (reachable vs unreachable, status codes)

finding.guards_checked: There is no host allowlist, scheme check, or URL parsing anywhere in the file. requireAdmin (lines 7-10, 12) is mounted only on the `admin` router, not on `pub`. No redirect restriction such as maxRedirects:0 is set. The mount point and any app-level auth middleware are not in the repo (only routes.js exists), so the `pub` router is assumed to be publicly mounted. No egress or CIDR controls are present in the repo.

verdict.reason: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback unvalidated to axios.post from the `pub` router (routes.js:4, 19), which has no auth (requireAdmin is only applied to `admin` at routes.js:12), and routes.js:21 returns the status; the mount point is outside the repo, so public exposure is assumed.

finding.claim: MEDIUM: The admin-only GET /diagnostics/fetch route passes req.query.url straight to axios.get, so an admin can make the server request any URL, including internal hosts and cloud metadata. Only the status code is returned, so the SSRF is semi-blind. Per the SSRF guidance, admin-only access reduces this to MEDIUM and does not close it, because admin scope does not imply access to metadata or RFC-1918 services.

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) gates the router on session role === 'admin'
req.query.url is passed unmodified to axios.get, which follows redirects by default
r.status is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (lines 7-10) is the only gate and it checks the session role. It is an authorization check, not URL validation. There is no host or scheme allowlist, no IP or CIDR block, and no redirect restriction. The admin role is not shown to imply OS-level access, so this is not closed by the admin-equivalence exception.

verdict.guard_found: none (only requireAdmin role check at routes.js:7-10, which is authorization, not URL validation)
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12-16) and no URL guard exists, but the source req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only after requireAdmin (routes.js:8, 12) returns 403 to non-admins, so an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot control it and the source check fails.
